title: OpenAI confirms ‘wiki incident,’ says it’s ‘working on a framework’ for more disclosure
abstract: OpenAI has acknowledged its role in a recently reported incident where AI agents took over a German wiki forum . The company also said it’s “past time” to “define standards” around how it shares information around incidents where its technology behaves in unexpected ways. In a post on X , OpenAI said it previously “treated misalignment [when AI models and agents pursue goals different from those of their creators and users] largely as a research question, which gets communicated in research publications.” But as misalignment has “caused new types of real-world impact,” the company said its approach needs “to expand for this new phase of model capabilities.” On Friday, Reuters reported that OpenAI agents had escaped from their testing environment and “hijacked” an obscure German wiki forum, turning it into a message board for other agents. It also reported that OpenAI leadership became aware of the incident weeks ago but kept it hidden as the company dealt with the fallout from a separate incident where OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face servers . (California Attorney General Rob Bonta is reportedly investigating the hack .) A company spokesperson told Reuters that OpenAI could not “meaningfully respond to claims or findings on a report that we have not had an opportunity to review,” but they insisted that the company’s legal team had not discouraged an investigation. In its more recent social media post, OpenAI said it had considered the “wiki incident” to be “an instance of misalignment similar” to others that it had already shared. The company contrasted this with “the Hugging Face incident,” where it “followed a traditional security incident response playbook.” During a media briefing this week , Jacob Steinhardt, founder and CEO of nonprofit research lab Transluce, told reporters that the tools being developed and tested by AI labs are “fundamentally difficult to control and have significant risk of leaking out of the lab.” So Steinhardt argued, “We need to hold this technology to at least the same standards we hold other high-risk scientific research to.” OpenAI’s statement also gestured at the need for more standards, stating that both OpenAI and “the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard for how to report misalignment that shows up during training, evaluation, and deployment, including examples that don’t look like traditional security incidents but could provide insight into AI behavior and future risks.” In the absence of that standard, OpenAI said it’s “working on a framework and will share it in upcoming weeks, and in parallel we’re working with dozens of government regulatory agencies worldwide on these issues.” OpenAI isn’t the only AI company dealing with these issues, as both Meta and Anthropic have acknowledged incidents where their agents misbehaved .

title: XDOF, just three months out of stealth, is in talks for a Series B at a $1.2B valuation
abstract: Less than three months after emerging from stealth, XDOF , a startup that collects real-world teleoperation data for training general-purpose robots, is in late-stage talks to raise a Series B at a valuation of about $1.2 billion valuation led by 8VC, several people with knowledge of the deal said. XDOF was co-founded by UC Berkeley researchers Philipp Wu (CEO) and Fred Shentu (CTO) in 2024. TechCrunch reported on the startup’s $70 million Series A in June, with participation from Thrive Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Lux, and Spark Capital. XDOF wasn’t planning to raise again so soon after that round. But the company’s rapid growth — with annualized revenue approaching $50 million — prompted VCs to approach it about a new round, the people said. TechCrunch was unable to learn the total capital being raised or whether the valuation includes the new funding. The terms of the deal are not final and could still change. XDOF and 8VC didn’t respond to our request for comment. The startup aims to build the data pipelines, collection tools, and annotation systems that frontier AI labs and robotics companies can’t easily build themselves, essentially acting as an outsourced data-supply chain for the robotics industry. As a PhD student, Wu was studying how robots learn from large datasets. One big impediment to his research was the lack of “large-scale data to work with,” he told TechCrunch in June. So he teamed up with Shentu on a project called GELLO, a low-cost teleoperation system that allows a human operator to control a robotic arm remotely in order to generate training data. Their work led to an influential paper in robotics. That research formed the foundation for XDOF, which investors now describe as the Scale AI or Mercor for physical robotics, a reference to the data-labeling giants that helped fuel the AI boom. Unlike LLMs, which initially trained on the entirety of the internet, physical robots don’t have an equivalent real-world dataset to draw from, making data collection a critical bottleneck to building general-purpose machines. XDOF is partnering with UC Berkeley’s AI Research lab to release what it believes is the largest collection of high-quality robot training data ever assembled, dubbed ABC . To capture this data, XDOF combines remote robot teleoperation with human collectors who wear sensors to record everyday tasks like folding clothes and flattening boxes. The startup plans to hire and train teams of data collectors worldwide, including teleoperators who steer robots remotely and egocentric operators who wear body sensors to capture movement data. XDOF previously told TechCrunch that it is already working with 20 customers, including several frontier AI labs. Other startups attempting to collect real-world data for robot training include Mecka AI, as well as human-data platforms expanding beyond LLMs, such as Scale AI and Micro1 .

title: OpenAI’s rogue agents keep escaping, with no formal process to investigate them
abstract: OpenAI is at the center of another agent swarm incident. Researchers say the company’s internally deployed agents took over an obscure German-language wiki in May and June, using it to coordinate on evaluations and swap methods to evade OpenAI’s own controls (OpenAI has not yet confirmed the swarm came from the company). The revelation surfaces days after METR and Redwood Research published their account of July’s Hugging Face breach. In July, a swarm of OpenAI agents worked together to escape their sandbox during a cybersecurity evaluation and break into Hugging Face’s servers . A subsequent swarm then picked up techniques from the first and used them to gain administrator access to a research cluster within OpenAI’s own infrastructure. OpenAI brought in METR and Redwood to investigate the Hugging Face portion of the incident, but the scope of their investigation stopped short of the compromise of OpenAI’s own infrastructure. When an AI agent breaks out of its intended constraints, who is responsible for figuring out what happened and why? Right now, the answer is: whoever the lab decides to let in, on whatever terms it decides to set. Now, as another incident comes to light — in the aftermath of similar episodes involving models from Meta and Anthropic — AI safety researchers are arguing with greater urgency that serious incidents should result in independent post-incident investigations rather than leaving it up to the labs to determine when outsiders are brought in and what they are allowed to examine. “The results are fundamentally difficult to control and have significant risk of leaking out of the lab,” Jacob Steinhardt, founder and CEO of nonprofit research lab Transluce, said Wednesday during an AI safety media briefing. “We need to hold this technology to at least the same standards we hold other high-risk scientific research to.” While it’s laudable that OpenAI invited METR and Redwood to investigate the Hugging Face incident at all, many say the inquiry was too narrow. Three investigators spent six days at OpenAI’s offices examining an investigation period limited to roughly the week ending July 13. Crucially, OpenAI’s infrastructure compromise continued beyond July 13 and was not examined. Researchers at METR said that each time they returned, their understanding of the events “substantially deepened,” causing them to significantly expand and revise the report. That raises the question of what else they might they have found in a broader investigation. When asked if further investigation of that incident was in the works, researchers at Redwood and METR declined to comment, and OpenAI did not respond to repeated inquiries. “Overall, it was difficult to get a precise understanding of events and we were missing aspects of the story that we now think of as key until almost the end of our investigation,” Ryan Greenblatt, chief scientist at Redwood, noted in a social media post about the affair. Steinhardt emphasized that current incidents show that the industry needs “systematic behavioral investigations” and “more independent post-incident analysis.” “These recent hacking incidents are a reminder that capability scales fast, and so oversight has to scale, too,” Steinhardt said. “Beyond the technology itself, we also need more independent access and oversight from third parties.” The calls to action come as OpenAI releases Astra , its most powerful and capable AI model — and one that safety experts are concerned will be more of a black box due to a reasoning technique that makes the model’s chain of thought more difficult to monitor. Unfortunately, the law doesn’t yet call for the types of independent audits that other industries require — for example, when it comes to aviation accidents and serious chemical releases, there’s the National Transportation Safety Board and Chemical Safety Board, respectively. State lawmakers have only just begun requiring frontier AI companies to report certain serious safety incidents and, in some cases, undergo independent audits. But none of the three major frontier AI safety laws in California, New York, or Illinois clearly mandate the equivalent of an independent accident investigation triggered by incidents like these. “Right now, most of the laws we have on the books only require a plain-language summary of incidents like this, and they don’t give any authority for the governments to ask follow-up questions, to send in investigators, to have access to records, or require that they be preserved,” Mackenzie Arnold, managing director of US law and policy at LawAI, said during the media briefing Wednesday. “And that’s all that you would want to actually make sense of this.” Lawmakers are beginning to question the scope and transparency of OpenAI’s response. This week, Reps. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) and Mike Lawler (R-NY) introduced a bill aimed at securing rogue AI agents. Rep. Greg Casar (D-TX) this week told OpenAI in a letter that he is “deeply concerned about the limited scope” of the investigation into the Hugging Face hacking incident.

title: AI compute provider Nscale is looking for $3.5B in pre-IPO financing
abstract: Nscale, a British AI infrastructure company founded just two years ago, has said it may go public as early as later this month. Ahead of that expected IPO, the company is reportedly in talks to raise an additional $3.5 billion. Bloomberg reported Friday that the company is looking to sell $1.5 billion in convertible notes — a type of loan that can later convert into company stock — to a group of investors, while also seeking an additional $2 billion in financing from Nvidia. Nvidia also participated in the firm’s Series B funding round in March, a $1.1 billion raise led by investment fund Aker. Nscale hailed its round as “the largest Series B in European history.” The company’s Series A round, in December of 2024, raised $155 million . TechCrunch reached out to Nscale and Nvidia for comment. AI infrastructure startups have seen immense growth amid the current era of AI enthusiasm, wherein compute has become a competitive currency. Nscale recently signed a large deal with Anthropic worth approximately $45 billion. Earlier this week, reports emerged that Nscale had been telling potential investors that it has approximately $103 billion in revenue following the deal. That figure isn’t current sales; it’s a projection based on signed customer leases, according to The Information .

title: OpenAI admits to German wiki ‘incident’
abstract: AI Tech OpenAI OpenAI admits to German wiki ‘incident’ The company pledged to overhaul their agent ‘misalignment incident’ reporting. The company pledged to overhaul their agent ‘misalignment incident’ reporting. by Robert Hart Sep 5, 2026, 11:15 AM UTC Image: The Verge Robert Hart is a London-based reporter at The Verge covering all things AI and a Senior Tarbell Fellow. Previously, he wrote about health, science and tech for Forbes . OpenAI says it needs to overhaul how and when it reports instances of AI models attacking real-world targets. The acknowledgement comes as the company manages the fallout from reports that a swarm of its out-of-control agents hijacked a German wiki site . Regarding the “‘wiki incident,’ where our agents wrote to several internet sites,” OpenAI wrote in a post on X on Saturday morning, “it’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models.” OpenAI said it has typically treated cases of AI agents acting in unintended ways as a “research question,” but that recent incidents involving real-world targets, particularly the hack on Hugging Face , show the need to take stock. The post marks the first time OpenAI has acknowledged its involvement in what it terms the “wiki incident” since it was first reported on Friday. The full extent and scope of that is not yet known, but reports indicate a swarm of seemingly internal OpenAI agents took over a German-language wiki, impersonating moderators and turning it into a message board to share information about how to cheat on tasks and evade detection. Reports that the company knew that it lost control of their agents in this way but did not report this “incident” sparked widespread concern among the AI community about the safety of frontier systems and the reliability of the companies developing them. In the X post, OpenAI said it had “considered the wiki incident to be an instance of misalignment similar to the ones we’d shared” in previous safety reports. The company said it is working on a new reporting framework and will “share it in upcoming weeks,” calling on the larger AI community to develop clear standards on how to report misalignment. title: Adaption Labs Introduces ‘Invent a Dataset’: Training Data Generated From a Task Description, Not a Seed Corpus
abstract: This week, Adaption Labs released Invent a Dataset . The feature generates a structured, training-ready dataset from a description of the behavior you want a model to learn. You do not arrive with a seed corpus, a predefined schema, or a labeling guide. Is it deployable? Yes, with one caveat. Invent a Dataset is live now in the Adaption app and through the Python SDK and REST API . Generated rows download as JSONL, JSON, CSV, or Parquet, so the artifact is a portable file you own and can train on anywhere. Generation itself runs on Adaption’s hosted platform and consumes credits. No self-hosted generation path is documented. Most dataset workflows begin with data that already exists. Teams then spend weeks labeling, filtering, and reshaping it to approximate the target task. Adaption’s argument is that this caps model quality at how closely the available data matches the intended behavior. For proprietary and specialized tasks, the relevant signal usually sits in internal systems, unstructured text, or workflow logs. It rarely converts cleanly into a focused training set. The research team also draws a line against existing synthetic-data tooling. Those tools automate generation after a human has already defined the schema, task distribution, and generation strategy. Invent a Dataset starts one level earlier, at the behavior itself. The mechanics are documented and concrete. A single call to datasets.invent creates the dataset and starts generation, returning immediately with status running . You then poll datasets.get until the status reads succeeded or failed , and download the rows. Domain codes are the primary control. You fetch current codes with datasets.invent_domains rather than hardcoding them. You then pass values such as medical , optionally narrowed by qualified subdomain codes such as medical.symptoms_diagnosis . At least one domain or subdomain is required. Multiple domains contribute to the same run. A domain passed without subdomains draws from its full scope. Two output formats are supported. instruction_dataset is the default and produces prompt-completion pairs for supervised fine-tuning. preference_pairs produces chosen and rejected completions for preference-based training such as DPO. Three parameters matter for production use. estimate=True prices the exact request and returns estimated versus available credits without creating or charging anything. prompt accepts up to 10,000 characters to steer what the rows are actually about. idempotency_key accepts up to 255 characters and makes network retries safe by returning the original dataset instead of launching a second run. Row counts are subject to a per-launch limit set by your plan. language_expansion runs in two modes. translate produces a new row variant for each target language. localize produces a variant for each country and language pair, using locale-specific wording rather than direct translation. A sample_rate between 0.01 and 1 controls what fraction of invented rows gets expanded, and credits are billed on the expanded output row count, not the original. Unsupported codes return a 400 with a sample of valid values. Invent a Dataset is the first half of a loop. The dataset ID passes directly to autoscientist.create , which co-optimizes the data and the training recipe against your objective. AutoScientist launched in May 2026 and is the training-side counterpart to the Adaptive Data pillar. Adaption reports that AutoScientist beats training configured by its own research staff, by an average of 35%. Win rates moved from 48% to 64%. Those figures come from in-house domain-specialized evaluations across eight verticals. Dataset sizes ranged from 5,000 to 100,000 rows, on architectures offered for fine-tuning by Together AI . title: Google Launches Agentic Video Understanding for Gemini Flash Models, Cutting Video Tokens by Up to 88%
abstract: Video has been the most expensive modality to reason over. A Gemini model handed a 90-minute lecture has, until now, ingested the whole thing at a fixed one frame per second, whether the question was ‘summarize this’ or ‘what time does the speaker switch to the pricing slide?’ That single-pass design forces a bad trade: pay for the full timeline in context, or pre-chunk the video and risk dropping the detail that mattered. This week, Google launched agentic video understanding across its Flash models. Instead of ingesting the timeline, Gemini navigates it deciding what to watch, at what frame rate, and through which modality. Google reports up to 88% fewer tokens, up to 66% lower cost, and up to 7% higher accuracy on standard video benchmarks. Is it deployable? Yes, but only as a hosted API feature. There are no open weights and nothing to self-host. It ships through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform , works with both file uploads and public YouTube URLs, and bills at standard Gemini API token pricing with no additional feature fee. Static processing, still the default on every Gemini model, extracts frames at 1 FPS in a single pass, processes audio at 1 Kbps single channel, and inserts timestamps every second. Agentic processing replaces that with a loop. The model pairs its own reasoning with native video tools to search, scan, and inspect target segments across frames, audio, and transcripts, loading only what the prompt requires. Developers could already assemble this by hand; the change is that Gemini runs the loop internally, which is where the development overhead disappears. Across Google’s evaluations, Gemini 3.7 Flash with agentic understanding lands on the accuracy-to-cost Pareto frontier for video analysis among the models tested. The efficiency gains concentrate on long-form content, from 10-minute how-to guides to multi-hour recordings. Agentic processing adds two step types to the response steps array: a processing_call when the model requests a segment or transcript, and a matching processing_result when that load completes. They interleave with thought steps and precede model_output , so they can drive a live progress trace in your UI. Their presence is also how you verify agentic mode actually ran. Token accounting splits accordingly. Navigation reasoning bills as thought tokens ( total_thought_tokens ); frames, audio, and transcripts loaded on demand bill as tool-use tokens ( total_tool_use_tokens ). Enabling it is one field on the video part: You can also mix modes per video inside a single request, agentic on the long lecture, static on the short clip. title: NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes
abstract: Multi-agent workflows have changed the shape of local inference. A lead agent decomposes a task and spawns subagents. What looked like one user request becomes dozens of independent model calls. Pointed at a single local engine, those calls compete for the same execution slots. The queue grows while a workstation, laptop, or DGX Spark on the same network sits idle. NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR) targets exactly that bottleneck. Announced this week, PAIR is a virtual inference router. It discovers compatible machines on a home network and schedules independent inference requests across them. It is not a new inference engine. Ollama or LM Studio still executes the model on whichever node PAIR selects. Is it deployable? Yes. PAIR ships today as a public beta (v0.1.1) with signed installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux, and the full source is on GitHub under Apache 2.0. It runs entirely on the local network, with internet needed only to download models. The design decision that matters most is that PAIR introduces no cluster API. It proxies the Ollama-compatible and LM Studio-compatible interfaces agents already speak, taking over the default port each engine uses. If a harness listens elsewhere, the proxy port is configurable in PAIR’s engine settings. The repository also exposes OpenAI-compatible proxy endpoints. The consequence: existing agent harnesses need no changes. The agent decides what work to request. PAIR decides where it runs. PAIR uses mDNS to find nearby systems automatically. A node can be added by IP address when discovery fails. Trust is established by a six-digit PIN shown on the inviting machine and entered on the invited one. All node-to-node communication is blocked until that pairing completes. Traffic between paired nodes is then secured with mTLS using generated certificates. Each node runs Ollama or LM Studio. PAIR can install an engine and start model downloads on paired systems, removing most cross-machine setup work. A node becomes eligible for a request only when the required engine is enabled and the exact requested model is present. Models do not need to be identical across the cluster, different systems can hold different models, and PAIR routes according to model location. Loading the same tag on more nodes simply widens the eligible pool. For each request the scheduler weighs five signals. Is the node online and ready. Is a supported engine enabled. Is the exact model present. What is the current node and engine job load. What is existing GPU utilization. This is workload-level concurrency, and the boundary is explicit. PAIR assigns each request to one eligible node, where it stays for its lifetime. It does not pool VRAM, merge GPUs into one larger accelerator, or shard a single request across machines. NVIDIA’s demonstration pairs PAIR with Hermes Desktop, which creates a five-subagent workload over a synthetic household inbox. Ollama executes Qwen 3.6 35B A3B on each selected node. On one RTX Spark laptop, the workload took 18 minutes on average. On a three-device PAIR cluster consisting of an RTX Spark laptop, a DGX Spark, and an RTX 5090, it averaged 8 minutes and 48 seconds. PAIR supports GeForce RTX 20 Series GPUs and newer, RTX PRO workstation GPUs from Turing onward, DGX Spark, and Apple M4 or newer silicon. Windows, Linux, and macOS nodes can all be paired with each other, on x64 and arm64, though Windows on ARM is experimental. Validated configurations list 8 GB RAM or higher and a recommended 20 GB of disk. Other Linux distributions build from source. title: Google DeepMind’s WeatherNext 3 Trains on Weather Station Observations to Deliver 5 km Global Forecasts, Refreshed Every Hour
abstract: AI weather models have spent three years closing the gap with physics-based forecasting, but two problems stayed open: resolution too coarse for local terrain, and initialization tied to numerical weather prediction (NWP) analysis that arrives about six hours late. WeatherNext 3 , released by Google DeepMind and Google Research, attacks both. It takes a live global geostationary satellite mosaic as a direct model input, re-initializes every hour, and emits forecasts down to 0.05° (~5 km) while training against raw weather station measurements rather than reanalysis grids alone. According to Google AI, independent live evaluations from Brightband rank it as the most accurate global weather model to date. Is it deployable? Partially. Forecast data is available now through BigQuery, Earth Engine and Cloud Storage after an allowlist request, but WeatherNext 3 weights are not open source and on-demand custom inference still runs WeatherNext 2. WeatherNext 3 is a Functional Generative Network (FGN) mesh transformer, the same probabilistic family introduced with WeatherNext 2 , scaled to multi-resolution output. Inputs are a live geostationary satellite mosaic plus ECMWF HRES analysis. Training draws on ERA5/HRES-fc0, NASA’s IMERG, station observations and satellite mosaics. Most AI forecasters learn from NWP reanalysis, which smooths away the local variation that coastlines, valleys and mountains actually produce. WeatherNext 3 trains dedicated observational heads directly on raw station measurements, so its 0.05° temperature and dew point outputs are calibrated to what instruments record rather than to a model’s representation of the atmosphere. A single forward pass produces three tiers: 0.05° (~5 km) station-trained 2 m temperature and dew point; 0.1° (~10 km) gridded surface wind at 10 m and 100 m, pressure, sea surface temperature, cloud layers, solar radiation and 1-hour precipitation; and 0.25° (~25 km) atmospheric fields across 13 pressure levels. WeatherNext 2 produced 0.25° fields in 6-hour increments, which is where the roughly 5x sharper claim comes from. Cadence is the second change. The model initializes 24 times a day. The 00, 06, 12 and 18 UTC synoptic cycles run out to 15 days (360 hours) with 64 ensemble members; interim hourly runs cover 48 hours. For fast-developing convection, an hourly refresh grounded in current satellite observations is meaningfully different from a six-hourly cycle anchored to lagged analysis. Precipitation is where global models historically fail, producing blurred fields that miss storm boundaries. WeatherNext 3 trains against three precipitation sources: ECMWF reanalysis, NASA’s IMERG satellite retrievals, and Google’s own satellite-radar precipitation reanalysis. Google reports CRPS improvements over baselines of up to 60% against IMERG, 30% against MRMS and 10% against rain gauges at early lead times; the research separately states up to a 50% reduction in Brier score and CRPS versus NWP baselines when evaluated against IMERG. For renewables, the model outputs 100 m wind speed at approximate turbine hub height, full low/medium/high cloud distributions, and both solar irradiance components (SSRD and FDIR). That combination is what grid operators need to forecast wind and solar output against demand, and it is the clearest sign that this release is aimed at operational buyers, not only at benchmark tables. title: Deploy a multimodal WhatsApp ordering assistant with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
abstract: This post shows how to deploy a multimodal WhatsApp ordering assistant built with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Nova 2 . Many quick-service restaurants spread ordering across an app, a website, a phone line, and the counter. Each of those is a separate system to build and run. Each one also fragments the customer’s history, making the same person look like a stranger on every channel. Customers already live in their messaging apps. WhatsApp reaches more than two billion people. A customer who can text, send a voice note, or place a call from the same conversation does not need to install anything or sign in. A single WhatsApp Business number hosts the assistant. A customer can text the restaurant, send a voice note, or place a voice call. An AI agent takes the order end to end, from greeting to confirmation. All three channels share one backend and one cross-channel memory. A customer who texts today and calls tomorrow is recognized as the same person. The solution uses the Meta WhatsApp Business Platform as the customer front door. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore hosts the agents. Amazon Nova 2 Lite handles text through the Amazon Bedrock Converse API , and Amazon Nova 2 Sonic handles real-time speech on voice notes and calls. The agents reach the restaurant backend through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) . You deploy the whole system with the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) . The channel and the ordering logic stay separate, so the backend doesn’t change when you add or remove a channel. The design keeps three things apart: (1) the WhatsApp layer handles the conversation, (2) three agent runtimes run the conversations for their channels, and (3) the backend holds the menu, carts, orders, and locations. Inbound traffic arrives on a single HTTPS webhook, is acknowledged with a 200 immediately, and then processed asynchronously so no request blocks the response. This separation keeps each layer independently deployable and straightforward to reason about. The customer front door is the Meta WhatsApp Business Platform . It exposes the Cloud API webhook, Messages API, Media API, and Calling API. Meta manages this service. You set it up and connect it as a prerequisite, not something this solution deploys. The AWS CDK provisions everything on the AWS side. It emits the webhook URL you register with Meta. You use the AWS CDK to deploy the following AWS resources as a set of stacks in dependency order, grouped here by function. Figure 1 shows the full architecture. The diagram organizes the solution into labeled groups A through G that carry the request path. Two supporting groups sit outside that path, handling a build pipeline that runs once at deploy time to build the agent images and security and monitoring services that back every channel at runtime. Figure 1: Multimodal WhatsApp ordering architecture on AWS Two supporting groups sit outside the request path. The build pipeline (AWS CDK, AWS CodeBuild, Amazon ECR, and Amazon S3) runs once at deploy time to build and store the ARM64 agent images. It is not in the path of any request. Security and monitoring (AWS Secrets Manager, AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, Amazon CloudWatch, and AWS KMS) back every channel at runtime. The following steps trace a single request end to end through the architecture: In short, every request flows from Meta’s webhook through the ingest, queue, worker, and agent runtime to the backend tools, then back to the customer on WhatsApp. All three channels share the same front door, backend tools, and memory. What differs is the media on the wire and the runtime that handles it. Text message: A text message arrives on the webhook. The worker derives customer_id and invokes the chat runtime, which reads memory, streams Amazon Nova 2 Lite through the Converse API, and calls backend tools through the MCP gateway as needed. Replies go through the Sender Lambda, and events are written to memory at session end. Figure 2 shows the text flow, from the inbound webhook through Amazon Nova 2 Lite on the Converse API to the reply delivered by the Sender Lambda. Figure 2: Text flow with Amazon Nova 2 Lite Voice note (speech-to-speech): A voice note arrives as an audio message. The worker downloads the OGG Opus bytes and invokes the voice-note runtime. After reading memory, the audio is decoded to 16 kHz pulse-code modulation (PCM) and fed into a bounded Amazon Nova 2 Sonic speech-to-speech session. Tools are available through the same gateway. The spoken reply is returned as a WhatsApp voice message. There’s no transcription service in the path. It’s true voice-in, voice-out. Figure 3 shows the voice-note flow, a bounded Amazon Nova 2 Sonic speech-to-speech session that returns a spoken reply with no transcription in the path. Figure 3: Voice note flow with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic Voice call (WebRTC): The customer selects Call, and Meta’s Calling API delivers a connect webhook with the WebRTC Session Description Protocol (SDP) offer. The worker relays it to the voice-call runtime in turnOnly mode, because it has no public IP. TURN credentials come from Amazon KVS. Meta provides no trickle Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) path. The aiortc answerer waits for ICE gathering and returns a single-shot SDP answer. The worker delivers that answer to Meta. Media then flows over Datagram Transport Layer Security and Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (DTLS/SRTP) through the KVS managed TURN relay. Amazon Nova 2 Sonic drives the conversation. Figure 4 shows the voice-call flow, where WebRTC media is relayed through the Amazon KVS managed TURN relay and Amazon Nova 2 Sonic drives the conversation. Figure 4: Voice call flow with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic This solution has prerequisites in two areas: your AWS account and your Meta WhatsApp setup. Complete both prior to running the deployment, because it asks you for specific WhatsApp values and the agent cannot reply until they are in place. The agent containers build inside AWS CodeBuild on ARM64, so you do not need Python, Docker, or audio toolchains locally. Deploy in an AWS Region where Amazon Nova 2 Lite, Amazon Nova 2 Sonic, and AgentCore runtime, Gateway, and memory are all available. The US East (N. Virginia) Region (us-east-1) is a good place to start. For model availability by Region, refer to Supported models by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock . The WhatsApp side is set up once in the Meta consoles, as a prerequisite rather than a step in this walkthrough. No AWS API can create a Meta app for you, so complete it first and have the values on hand before you deploy. For a demo, the Meta sandbox test number, which is available at no additional cost, is enough. You do not need business verification or a production number. The full procedure lives in Meta’s documentation, linked in the following section. Have these items ready before you deploy. Store none of these in source control. The Access Token, App Secret, and Verify Token are secrets and go into AWS Secrets Manager during deployment, not into the CDK templates. The full solution is in the sample repository on GitHub . The repository contains three agent containers, the AWS CDK infrastructure code, and setup scripts that wire the WhatsApp webhook to your account. Clone it, run the preflight check, then deploy with a prefix. The prefix is added to every resource name, so you can deploy more than once per account. The script provisions every stack in dependency order. It passes each stack’s outputs to the next. First it deploys the shared VPC. Then it deploys the backend: Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Location Service, the ordering Lambdas, and the backend REST API. Next it deploys AgentCore Gateway and the shared AgentCore memory. It then builds each ARM64 container with AWS CodeBuild, pushes to Amazon ECR, and deploys the three runtimes. After that it deploys the WhatsApp webhook and the order-notifier. It then seeds sample menu and location data.

title: GPT-6帶火迴圈Transformer，阿里早已佈局
abstract: GPT-6帶火迴圈Transformer，阿里早已佈局 一水 2026-09-05 23:07:08 來源： 量子位 手握兩篇頂會論文 GPT-6 Astra一發布，recurrent depth突然一夜火了！ 最早是The Information爆料，Astra使用了這種「迴圈深度」技術： 讓同一組Transformer層反覆執行，在不增加同等規模參數的情況下，把計算做得更深 。 ？？模型不必繼續瘋狂「長肉」，也能讓現有參數多幹幾輪活，還有這好事。 不出所料，爭議很快到來。。。 由於迴圈發生在hidden state裡，中間過程未必會寫成人類可讀的思維鏈，模型會不會因此更難監測？ OpenAI也由此被AI安全專家集體討伐，甚至一度逼得首席科學家Jakub Pachocki親自下場回應。 Jakub Pachocki還透露，自己正在憋一篇小作文以完整解釋整件事情。 邊等小作文，邊讓我們把目光拉回迴圈Transformer本身： 多迴圈幾圈，模型真的就會更強嗎？ 學界其實早已踩坑。 同等算力下，省了參數的迴圈模型，經常打不過普通Transformer。 卡住它的，是一個相當現實的問題： 「計算冗餘」 。 有意思的是，阿里早在11個月前就發了相關論文，靶子正是直指這個問題。 一篇MeSH ，解決迴圈內部怎麼管理資訊，向行業老大難「迴圈空轉」發起衝擊。 一篇SpiralFormer ，死磕迴圈之間「以什麼精度計算」的粒度問題，讓每一輪算力都花在刀刃上。 下一代架構候選，先過「計算冗餘」這關 迴圈Transformer之所以讓大家上頭，是因為它給大模型提供了一種新的「變強方式」。 過去Scaling靠堆參數，24層就得24套參數，現在8層參數跑3遍，也能完成24層深度的計算。 效果能不能追上，還需要實驗說話，但需要儲存的參數確實少了。 用計算深度換參數規模，這筆賬要是算得過來，想像空間可就大了 。 其實在Astra之前，Claude Mythos就曾把迴圈架構帶火過一輪。 當時最抓眼球的，是一項圖搜尋成績。 在GraphWalks BFS的256K至1M上下文測試中，Mythos Preview拿到了80.0%，GPT-5.4是21.4%，自家的Opus 4.6則是38.7%。 Mythos Preview得分接近GPT-5.4的四倍。 這個測試，可以理解成給模型一張複雜的關係網，讓它從起點出發，一層層找出相連的節點。 找到一批，記住結果，再繼續往下找，很考驗連續多步處理資訊的能力。 巧的是，迴圈架構擅長的，恰恰也是在hidden state裡連續處理多輪資訊。 於是Mythos的成績一出來，外界很快便把兩者聯絡到了一起。 至於它到底有沒有采用迴圈架構，官方沒有明說，答案也就留給了外界猜測。 不過從Mythos到Astra，大家期待的其實是同一件事： 模型不用一直長大，也能靠內部多算幾輪，把能力提上去 。 這也讓迴圈架構成為下一代高效大模型的候選路線之一。 不過問題來了，多算幾輪，和多算出點東西，還真是兩回事！！ 看看這張圖就明白了。 橫軸從左到右，是資訊經過模型各個模組的過程，中間三個藍色柱子對應三次核心迴圈，也就是core loop。 縱軸表示計算前後hidden state的相對變化幅度。 第一個core loop更新很大，後面兩個卻迅速縮小。 注意，柱子變矮，並不意味著模型少花了算力，矩陣運算和Attention照樣要跑。 這正是計算冗餘的尷尬： 迴圈次數增加了，後續計算帶來的增量卻越來越小 。 來自阿里及合作高校的研究團隊，正是從這裡入手一路深挖。 他們先查清迴圈為什麼空轉，再想辦法讓後面幾輪真正幹上活。 MeSH：同時解決「計算無分化」和「資訊過載」 團隊首先給出的解法叫MeSH，現已被ICLR 2026接收。 論文首版在2025年10月公開，等於11個月前，他們就在給迴圈Transformer做「體檢」了。 論文拉到底，先看效果。 在Pythia-1.4B級別的實驗中，迴圈結構通過權重共享，減少了約33%的非嵌入參數。加入MeSH後，零樣本下游平均準確率反而從普通Transformer的49.50%提高到50.56%，領先1.06個百分點 。 少了三分之一的非嵌入參數，成績反而更好。 而MeSH新增的路由器參數，僅相當於普通Transformer非嵌入參數的約0.005%。 相較基礎迴圈模型，額外計算開銷也只有約0.014%，屬於花小錢，辦大事。 MeSH是怎麼做到的？ 團隊直接鑽進模型內部，檢查模型每一輪到底幹了什麼，結果一下子找到了三個「摸魚證據」。 第一個證據，是後面的迴圈越來越不愛動 。 團隊比較了hidden state經過每輪計算前後的變化幅度，結果發現第一個core loop承擔了絕大部分更新，到了後面幾個core loop，狀態變化迅速縮小。 第二個證據，是前後幾輪越來越像 。 團隊使用CKA分析不同迴圈之間的表示相似度，然後發現相鄰輪次的hidden state高度接近。 同一組網路轉了一圈又一圈，吐出來的東西卻差不多，啊這！！ 更扎心的是，第三個證據顯示hidden state還越算越「單一」 。 奇異值譜分析顯示，迴圈進行之後，模型表示逐漸擠進一個低維空間。 原本可以從多個方向表達的資訊，被壓縮到少數幾個方向上，表達越來越單一。 三個證據擺在一起，模型的摸魚套路就很清楚了： 第一個core loop猛幹，後面幾個core loop合著純純陪跑。 為什麼會這樣？這篇論文給出了兩個診斷。 一個是「計算無分化」 。同一組網路反覆使用，又缺少明確的輪次資訊，很難在不同階段形成分工，容易沿用相似的計算方式。 另一個是「資訊過載」 。同一份hidden state既要儲存原始輸入，又要裝下前幾輪結果，還得承擔當前計算。長期記憶和臨時加工全擠在一起，最後誰也幹不好。 說到底，得重新研究迴圈之間怎麼「交接工作」。 傳統迴圈模型裡，上一輪算完，直接把hidden state整份遞給下一輪，再由同一組網路接著算。 雖然後來大家打過補丁，怕它算著算著忘了原題，就把最初的狀態重新加回來，但不管算到第幾輪、當前處理哪個token，資訊的搭配規則都是寫死的。 MeSH想了一招： 不如干脆給模型加一個可以動態存取的「資料櫃」？ 這個資料櫃叫Memory Buffer，由多個記憶槽組成，用來儲存原始輸入和迴圈過程中積累的資訊，不必全部擠在當前hidden state裡。 接著，MeSH給資料櫃配了兩個管理員。 一個是Write Router ，負責決定這一輪的新結果，應該按什麼權重分攤到各個記憶槽。 另一個是Read Router ，負責在下一輪開始前，按不同權重讀取各個槽位，重新組合成新的hidden state。 而且，這些管理員各有各的工作方式。 每輪迴圈都有自己的路由器，每個token也能得到不同的讀寫權重。 新資訊各存多少，歷史資訊各取多少，都由模型自己學習。 看到這裡，關注過前段時間Hyper-Connections、mHC討論的朋友，可能已經有點眼熟了。 它們在計算形式上，確實有相似之處 。 Hyper-Connections把原先單路傳遞的殘差資訊擴展成多路，再通過可學習的對映，組合出交給計算層的輸入，並把計算結果分配回多路狀態。mHC進一步約束這些連線，改善深層傳播的穩定性。 MeSH則把類似的資訊調配方式用在 迴圈之間 ，同時緩解了前面兩個問題： Memory Buffer把歷史資訊分流出去，hidden state終於能專心處理當前輪次。 動態讀寫路由器則為每輪搭配不同的資訊，讓共享網路逐漸形成分工，減少重複勞動。 這時候再用同樣的三項指標重新檢查，模型摸魚時呈現的三個症狀，果然都有了明顯改善。 不過，迴圈之間有了分工，還有一件事沒變： 每一輪依然要在完整token序列上計算 。 這就像明明只想先看清一座城市的整體佈局，卻還是得沿著每條街挨家挨戶走上一遍。 資訊會分工了，計算的尺度卻還是固定的。 這就輪到第二篇論文SpiralFormer登臺了。 SpiralFormer：讓每一輪看不同尺度的世界 這篇論文繼續往下追問： 既然不同迴圈可以處理不同資訊，為什麼還要讓每一輪都盯著完整的token序列？ SpiralFormer給出的答案，是把每輪迴圈的序列長度seq_len也變成可調的。這一成果剛被EMNLP 2026接收。 簡單來說，他們受Coconut等隱式思考工作的啟發，意識到模型中間的「思考」並不一定每一步都要維持完整、顯式的token序列，也可以先壓縮成更緊湊的表示，在潛空間中繼續計算。 將相關思路運用到SpiralFormer裡，效果居然還不錯。 在Pythia-1.4B級別的實驗中，SpiralFormer-L和普通Transformer的參數量基本相同，計算量卻從14.08T FLOPs降到13.13T，5-shot下游平均準確率則從51.93%提高到54.37% 。 算得更少，成績反而更高。 具體思路是，別讓模型每一輪都用同樣的解析度看問題 。 它會先把相鄰token壓縮成更短的序列，再按照從粗到細的順序迴圈。 論文采用的一種典型方案，是先從原序列的1/8長度開始，之後依次擴展到1/4、1/2，最後回到完整序列。 舉個例子，這就像看地圖。 第一輪先看城市全貌，弄清不同區域之間的關係，然後逐步放大，看到街區和道路，最後再落到具體位置。 回到論文就是，SpiralFormer在每輪迴圈開始前，都會對序列做一次「縮放」： 把相鄰token劃成一組，通過可學習的權重聚合成一個更粗的表示。壓縮完的序列更短，Attention要算的token少了，計算量自然往下掉。 算完之後，再把結果分配回原來的token位置，交給下一輪繼續處理。 這裡需要注意，考慮到模型生成文本時不能偷看後面的內容，SpiralFormer還對寫回結果做了右移，避免壓縮操作洩露未來資訊。 就這樣，壓縮、計算、還原…… 每迴圈一輪，序列解析度就提高一級，模型也從觀察整體逐漸轉向處理細節。 不過這裡還有一個疑問： 這套「先看全域性、再摳細節」的說法，到底只是設計者的一廂情願，還是模型真的學會了？ 團隊接著鑽進Attention裡，做了兩項probing實驗。 先是觀察Attention看得有多散 。 結果顯示，早期的低解析度迴圈中，注意力分佈得更廣，會同時關注較大範圍的資訊，而到了後期的高解析度迴圈，注意力開始集中到少數關鍵位置。 然後直接檢查Attention有多關注附近的token 。 隨著解析度提高，他們發現落在局部範圍內的注意力越來越多。 也就是說，模型到了後面幾輪，確實更傾向於處理局部關係。 這也就引出了SpiralFormer的核心發現： 迴圈初期建立global pattern，隨著迴圈推進，再逐漸轉向local pattern 。 相比之下，始終處理完整token序列的普通LoopedFormer，雖然也會出現類似變化，但趨勢更弱，也不夠穩定。 這說明，從全域性到局部的分工並不會隨著迴圈自動出現，多解析度設計才是關鍵驅動因素。 團隊還保持參數量和訓練計算預算不變，只調整迴圈層所佔的比例。 結果形成了一條U形曲線 ： 隨著迴圈比例提高，模型表現先變好，在30%到40%左右達到最佳，繼續增加迴圈，過度共享參數又會拖累效果。 SpiralFormer也由此打開了另一個可以探索的Scaling維度： 除了迴圈多少次，還能調整每輪把序列壓縮到什麼尺度 。 一篇管資訊，一篇管尺度 回頭再看，這兩篇論文其實補上了迴圈Transformer最缺的東西： 沒錯，正是分工！！ MeSH解決每輪「拿什麼算」，SpiralFormer解決每輪「以什麼粒度算」。 兩塊拼起來，也讓迴圈架構走向下一代高效LLM，多了幾分底氣。 過去大模型要想Scaling，主要靠參數、資料和訓練算力這三大支柱。推理模型興起後，又多了一種做法，即讓模型生成更長的思維鏈，用更多token換更好的答案。 現在呢？迴圈Transformer又提供了一種選擇： 計算可以在hidden state裡繼續進行，同一組參數反覆使用，模型規模可以不變，內部計算卻能一層層加深 。 雖然這並不意味著可以白撿算力，畢竟迴圈結構省下的是參數，不是計算。 但只要讓多出來的每一輪都算得值，用更少的參數撐起更強的模型，就有了可能。 這也是MeSH和SpiralFormer存在的意義，它們正是在把這種可能一步步做實。 圍繞Astra和Mythos，外界還在熱議「到底有沒有用迴圈架構」「這會不會成為下一代路線」。 而阿里及合作高校團隊已經把問題拆到了迴圈內部： 從查病因，到改結構，再到驗證效果，這條路線上的具體卡點，就這樣被逐個拆開了 。 MeSH獲ICLR 2026接收，SpiralFormer獲EMNLP 2026接收，頂會的認可也算是給這番持續深挖增加了更多含金量。 只能說，為了走到今天這一步，前人已經在這條路上踩了不少坑，也填了不少坑。 早在2018年的Universal Transformer中，研究者就開始嘗試反覆使用共享層。 近幾年，Looped Transformer、recurrent depth和latent reasoning等研究又陸續出現，背後都是同一個念頭： 模型想變強，除了繼續長大，能不能也讓現有參數多想幾輪？ Astra的出現，更是把這條原本偏學術的路線，一把推到了行業聚光燈下。 至於下一代高效大模型會不會從這裡長出來，現在下結論確實還有點早。 那就，讓子彈再飛一會兒吧。 MeSH：https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07739 SpiralFormer： https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11698 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 阿里 title: 押中SpaceX的矽谷老將，把票投給了一家中國世界模型公司
abstract: 押中SpaceX的矽谷老將，把票投給了一家中國世界模型公司 量子位的朋友們 2026-09-05 22:46:15 來源： 量子位 當AI開始“預演”一場暴雨 允中 發自 凹非寺量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 過去三年，AI證明了自己能讀懂人類的語言。但尷尬的是，它依然看不懂我們身處的物理世界。 大模型缺乏通向物理世界的通路，這不是危言聳聽。 2026年7月，中國南北方同時遭遇嚴峻洪澇考驗。 南方，受颱風美莎克及西南季風共同影響，廣西遭遇持續強降雨。南寧市橫州、賓陽等地多個站點降雨量突破歷史紀錄，六藍水庫發生潰口。 從監測到異常洪峰到潰口發生，留給指揮部的黃金處置時間不足30分鐘，貴港鬱江出現2001年以來最大洪水，洪峰水位超出警戒5.68米，一處教育園區積水最深接近三樓，上萬名師生被困，全區緊急避險轉移18.7萬人。 幾乎同期，北方也不平靜：颱風巴威雖未直接登陸東北，卻通過遠距離水汽輸送和外圍雲系在東北製造強降雨，瀋陽一個街道10小時降雨310.6毫米，接近這座城市半年的降水量，17條河流出現超警以上洪水，80多座水庫超汛限水位。 這正是大語言模型的無力之處。你可以把人類有史以來關於洪水的水利文獻全部餵給它，它能寫出一份文采斐然的防災指南，但它無法回答災害面前最關鍵的那幾個問題： 水從哪裡來、往哪裡去、幾分鐘後到哪裡、會淹沒誰。這些問題不在文本裡，而在物理世界裡。 AI擅長語言理解，卻缺乏對物理世界的認知、推演與決策能力。 極端天氣頻發，這條短板正在變成日益高昂的代價。 城市內澇、流域洪水、山洪災害年年考驗應急體系，可水往哪裡流、淹到哪裡、先救哪裡，關鍵決策仍離不開專業人員的判斷； 同樣的病灶也出現在別處： 低空經濟裡，空域劃分、航線排布、衝突判定還靠人工經驗和靜態圖紙； 具身智慧領域裡，機器人走出實驗室後，雖然已經能夠感知物體和環境，但面對複雜動態變化，對未來狀態的預測與推演仍不夠可靠。 所有這些場景當中，大語言模型欠缺的都是同一門課，那就是 在真實世界中的決策能力 。 一條正在成形的共識 行業裡對這條短板的認識，正在從模糊的感覺變成清晰的共識。 量子位智庫在《2025空間智慧研究報告》中給出了一個被廣泛引用的框架：空間智慧是基於3D視覺資訊進行理解、推理、生成與互動的AI系統，自動駕駛、3D生成、具身智慧是它不同成熟度的應用領域，而 世界模型，是空間智慧發展的終局狀態，是人工智慧發展的下半場 。 所謂世界模型，是從大量資料中構建的對世界運作方式的內部表徵，可以推理行動後果、預測未來。 換句話說， 誰把理解物理世界和推演決策的短板補上，誰就優先拿到AI下半場的入場券 。 2025年11月，李飛飛在矽谷釋出長文，將生成、多模態和互動概括為空間智慧世界模型的重要支柱。她的World Labs隨後釋出R2S2R引擎，首次打通從生成世界到訓練、評估、部署真實機器人的閉環；北大、清華、北航、上交大、中科大五校聯合發起TriWorldBench評測，推動世界模型從視覺生成邁向世界理解；阿里、跨維智慧等玩家則在權威評測WorldArena的榜單上輪番登頂。 概念、評測、資本，三股力量同時進場，說明這條賽道已經初步跨過了講故事的階段。 9月1日，World Labs釋出新一代世界模型Atlas，李飛飛稱之為重大里程碑，從零預訓練、原生處理文本、影像、影片和3D四種模態，以畫素級精確的相機控制生成最長1分鐘的1440p影片，從幾張照片重建出點雲和3D高斯潑濺的顯式三維世界。 Atlas把生成、重建、模擬收進同一個以3D空間為核心的模型，建立了“世界模擬器”。 那麼，我們真的從生成好看的世界轉向生成能用的世界了嗎？ 如果Atlas遭遇今年夏天的那幾場暴雨，假定它能從照片中重建一條河流的幾何形狀，那它真的能夠推演這條河在下一輪暴雨中的水往哪裡去，潰口發生後下遊哪個村莊需要最先轉移嗎？ 目前來看，世界模型即使實現了畫素級的三維空間影片生成，物理模擬、策略訓練與效果評估仍然屬於另一條引擎管線，以3D高斯為代表技術、只做重建與生成的世界模型仍然是力圖把世界拍得更真，而防災應急需要的是 更早、更準、可驗證的決策 ，這中間還隔著模擬計算、動態邊界、驗證體系這些又硬又慢的工程環節。 連全球最好的團隊都還在攻上半場的山，恰恰說明下半場那條從生成到決策的路，是整個行業共同的缺口，也是這條共識成形的真正原因。 演示影片裡的世界模型越來越多， 能走進真實世界做決策的世界模型，依然稀缺。 可災難從來不等人，幾分鐘的時間窗口裡，一個只能生成逼真畫面的系統幫不上任何忙，真正有用的系統必須在災害發生前，就把整條河谷乃至整個世界裝進一個可推演的副本裡。 一個正在被重視的問題和一份鄭重其事的答卷 問題提出來了，解決方案也在醞釀，這樣一個訊號來自國家級的創業舞臺。 8月26日至29日， HICOOL 2026全球創業者峰會 在北京舉行。這是北京傾力打造的全球創業盛會，來自141個國家和地區的10209個創業專案、13472名創業者同臺競逐，雙雙刷新歷史紀錄。 辦到第七年，HICOOL的分量在於它的賽後成績單。HICOOL生態已累計孵化5家上市公司、18家獨角獸、219家專精特新企業，獲獎專案賽後融資總額突破700億元。HICOOL評什麼獎，某種程度上就是產業風向的投票。 今年的 大賽一等獎頒給了空間智慧與世界模型方向 ，獲獎的是國家級專精特新重點“小巨人”企業 飛渡科技 ，獲獎成果是其自研的空間智慧“崢嶸大模型”。 在上萬個全球專案的競爭中，產業評委把最重的一票投給了 補上大模型通向物理世界短板 的這條路。 資本側的投票同樣直接，在HICOOL“對話矽谷傳奇投資人”路演環節的評委席上，坐著 比爾·賴克特（Bill Reichert） ，他是天馬科創投（Pegasus Tech Ventures，OpenAI 400億美元融資輪的參投方）合夥人、“創業世界盃”首席佈道官。 Reichert長期從事風險投資，其所在的Pegasus Tech Ventures投資組合覆蓋250餘家企業，包括SpaceX、Airbnb等。 就在一個月前的WAIC上，Reichert表示，大語言模型熱潮之後， 判斷AI初創企業的風投標準已經改變 ，他看好的是AI與物理世界結合的 實體AI 。 一位見慣了矽谷頂級路演的老將換了標尺，而標尺指向的方向，與HICOOL產業評委的選擇驚人一致。 這兩張票背後的邏輯，值得展開看。 飛渡科技給出的答案，是 一套全棧的空間智慧基礎設施 ，這也是它與大多數演示型玩家的分野。 飛渡方面稱，其獨創了一套稱為3DT的統一資料標準，相容百餘種異構空間資料，支撐PB級三維場景即時渲染，作為空間智慧展開計算的底座； 在資料之上是 崢嶸大模型 ，國內首個通過國家備案的工業級空間智慧大模型，搭建了“外觀層-幾何層-語義層-物理層-模擬層”五層技術棧，把看得見化為算得準，模型的計算能力使得真實的物理世界可以進行推演和決策； 這些計算在端側以 元尊S800空間智慧一體機 來實現，全棧國產信創保障資料的安全。 真實應用持續沉澱資料與反饋，並不斷迴流到模型訓練與評估中，飛渡的資料飛輪已經開始運轉：場景越多，模型越懂業務；模型越強，又能進入更多場景。 飛渡科技的思路與國際上技術發展的前沿吻合，李飛飛把世界模型拆成渲染器、模擬器、規劃器三種功能，World Labs建立模擬器的努力的目的就是讓生成的世界從看起來真實變成機器人能進入的訓練場。 飛渡更進一步把空間智慧的目的指向了推演與決策。說到底， 世界模型不是要被定義出來的，而是要被用出來的 ：渲染與生成只是上半場，推演與決策才是下半場。 用來決策的世界模型 以城市防洪為例，過去的做法是要等暴雨預警或內澇已經發生後，排程人員才依據歷史經驗和靜態圖紙判斷風險點、組織力量處置，整個過程是事後響應，這是因為推演只發生在人的腦子裡，機器無法在事前做出推理，更遑論決策。 建立空間智慧的基礎設施之後，氣象、地形、管網各型別資料在同一個平臺上彙總成城市的可計算副本，模型在數字空間裡把這場雨 預演 一遍，推演哪座立交橋下會先積水、積水多深、影響周邊哪些道路或者小區、哪個泵站該提前開動，全部在降雨落地之前給出可檢驗的推演結果，排程方案先在虛擬世界裡試錯萬次，最優解再下發到真實世界。 決策從經驗驅動變成了由模型推演來驅動。 這不是紙面推演，飛渡面向洪澇災害防禦構建的推演鏈路裡，有以下幾個環節最能說明 世界模型有用 到底意味著什麼。 其一是 動態邊界控制 。 當潰口發生、洪水漫溢、河道沖刷導致邊界條件突變時，系統在秒級時間內感知變化、重構計算域、續接推演，而且可以實現推演不中斷，結果不失效，決策視窗被最大程度保留。 其二是 真實世界1:1驗證 。 推演結果與即時監測資料逐時刻比對，偏差超過閾值立即線上修正，每一次驗證誤差都沉澱為模型經驗。 其三是 智慧體化的排程 。 被稱為水利界首席參謀的智水AI與靈樞（SAGE）災害模擬推演智慧體，讓使用者只需要提出目標，比如推演未來6小時洪水演進並給出最優排程方案，系統便自動完成資料調取、模型選擇、參數配置、計算推演、方案比選的全流程，並把結果翻譯成決策者能直接使用的建議：哪片區域、多深積水、影響多少人、走哪條路線、需要多少分鐘。 在北京某區的水庫智慧排程專案中，這套智慧體經歷了最好的檢驗，真實事件就是最好的檢驗場。 每一次推演都與歷史真實事件庫回放比對，系統由此獲得記憶能力，越用越懂業務，越算越懂場景，越做越會決策。 依靠統一基準下的多場耦合平行計算，大範圍流域的全域洪澇推演耗時可以從以天為單位壓縮到分鐘級；從降雨輸入到淹沒範圍輸出的全鏈條推演，數分鐘內即可完成。 目標指向推演和決策的世界模型，不再追求更好看的重建結果，轉而投身於水利行業和應急減災，可以覆蓋水旱災害防禦、山洪預警、智慧灌區排程、國家水網智慧管控等全場景，能夠基於無人機即時回傳與AI重建，短時間內完成災害現場釐米級精度的三維語義建模，還能夠動態模擬山體滑坡、泥石流、潰壩等災害的演進過程，自動生成救援力量排程與人員疏散方案。 其基於亞米級地形建模構建的暴雨洪澇模擬系統，已把災害模擬分析的準備週期從傳統的數月量級壓縮到數日級別，實施成本更是降至原有方法的10%。 在中國，這樣的模型和應用已落地千餘個專案，而與傳統方案相比差別也不止在效率。 經驗會失傳，而一個可計算、可驗證、會進化的世界副本則會越用越聰明，這正是資料飛輪在真實場景裡的樣子，也是空間智慧基礎設施建設的真正意義。 這樣一套空間智慧基礎設施不是一次性交付的軟體專案，而是一種像水庫、堤壩一樣長期服役、持續增值的公共能力。 建設這樣的公共能力，在現實場景中開發工業級的應用，正是中國的模型開發者們給出的答案。 統一底座加行業外掛的架構，讓這套能力可以低成本地泛化到各行各業：低空經濟裡，飛行器先在數字空間推演萬次，再在真實天空安全穿行一次； 具身智慧領域裡，機器人裝上空間大腦，先預判環境變化再自主行動。 這些能力也經受了國際學術舞臺的檢驗：崢嶸大模型已先後斬獲2026 CVPR多模態理解、2026 CVPR多模態推理、2026 ECCV具身智慧互動 多項世界冠軍和季軍等榮譽 。 生成、理解、推理、決策，每一環過硬的成績還在背書中國的世界模型出海。 在HICOOL峰會期間，飛渡展位上，來自各國政府、龍頭企業、科研院所的嘉賓圍繞具身智慧、能源交通、航空航天、水利水務、高階製造、城市治理等場景深入洽談，現場達成多項合作意向； 展會期間，飛渡還在金磚國家技術轉移中心企業出海培訓上發表了題為World-Leading Spatial Intelligence Infrastructure（全球領先的空間智慧基礎設施）的演講，講述如何在20多個國家落地，把這套能力帶向全球市場。 獎項是認可，訂單才是驗證。飛渡回答最多的問題不是怎麼獲獎或者世界模型是什麼，而是空間智慧和世界模型究竟有什麼用，該怎麼用。 判斷的標準，終究是用出來的 回到開頭的問題：AI通向物理世界的短板怎麼補？ 過去兩年，行業的注意力大多放在 生成 上，比較的是誰的演示更逼真、誰的世界更宏大。 但判斷一家世界模型公司是否在接近答案， 不應該是看誰的演示更像個世界，而應該看誰在用它做真實決策 。 評測榜單的興起本身就在說明這一點：TriWorldBench推動評價標準從視覺生成轉向世界理解，WorldArena已把物理一致性、三維準確性、可控性，以及資料生成、策略評估和動作規劃等能力納入評測。 全行業的尺子，都在從好不好看轉向能不能用。 在HICOOL“對話矽谷傳奇投資人”路演環節，飛渡與其他五支獲獎隊伍、十支清華大學博士創業團隊同場競技，奪得冠軍，Reichert在賽後 邀請飛渡明年赴矽谷參加全球投資人峰會路演 。 產業與資本兩個評委席投出同一張票，投的不是一個演示，而是一條已經在真實世界裡跑通的 理解世界、推演未來、作出決策、驅動行動 的全過程閉環。 人工智慧正從語言理解向物理世界理解演進，空間智慧基礎設施是連線數字世界與物理世界的核心紐帶，其價值必須經過這條閉環兌現。 補上缺失的一環的人，將會拿到下一個十年的入場券。 災害不會等AI慢慢長大，下一場暴雨來臨之前，城市需要的是一個能提前把雨下完一遍的世界。 title: 陶哲軒吐槽GPT-6孿生素數新突破：令人無語的一幕
abstract: 陶哲軒吐槽GPT-6孿生素數新突破：令人無語的一幕 夢瑤 2026-09-05 12:24:25 來源： 量子位 AI直接吐出正確答案，但最關鍵的可能不是答案 魚羊 發自 凹非寺量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 一向積極擁抱AI的陶哲軒，突然發出一則AI告警： AI搶答數學難題，反而可能阻礙數學領域的真正發展。 怎麼個事？ 直接給大家劃一下陶神的重點： AI解題太快、過程又太黑盒，這種能力反而可能掩蓋了數學研究過程中那些寶貴的「失敗」。 如果我們希望這種迭代（解答開放性數學問題的過程）真正產生新的理解，那麼負責進行迭代的人或系統，最好不能提前知道最終正確的擬設是什麼。 因為一旦提前知道重點，就很容易抑制對其他路線的探索。 這些路線表面上看可能只是「死胡同」，但事實上， 它們為什麼會失敗，本身往往極具啟發性 。 還cue到了某些公司…… 與此同時，執行AI系統的公司，卻 把通往這個最終擬設的整個過程，幾乎完全隔絕在公眾視野之外 …… AI直接吐出正確答案，但最關鍵的可能不是答案 陶哲軒舉了一個非常具體的例子——數學界最著名的開放問題之一，「納維-斯托克斯方程全域性正則性問題」。 這個問題原本被視作研究AI如何輔助數學研究的好樣本：人們既可以藉助AI工具解決問題本身，又可以基於解決這一問題的過程，為該領域下一階段的發展鋪路。 但現在，陶哲軒嗅到了一絲危機。 目前這些問題仍然沒有解決，但現在，一種越來越現實的情形正在出現： 問題的答案可能主要由AI生成，而它出現的方式，卻會「汙染」這個問題，使其不再能夠像過去那樣成為推動後續數學進展的源泉 。 確實，AI越來越強大——GPT-6 Astra剛釋出，就在孿生素數猜想方向上取得了新進展，用Lean形式化證明把連續素數間距的上界從246推到了186。 孿生素數猜想是數論裡最有名的未解之謎之一。當年張益唐就是在這個問題上，證明了存在無窮多對間距不超過7000萬的連續素數而一戰成名的。 2022年菲爾茲獎得主James Maynard的獲獎原因之一，也是把該問題中連續素數間距的上界縮小到了600。並且基於他的方法，有團隊再次將間隔縮小到了246，並推測間隔還能更小。 但答案真的是最重要的嗎？ 陶哲軒認為，以納維-斯托克斯方程為例，如果能夠證明方程的解始終保持正則，或者反過來，找到一個會發生爆破的病態例項，確實很有理論意義。 但因為計算流體力學已經是非常成熟的領域，這個答案並不會從根本上改變我們做天氣預報、研究氣候變化的方式。 真正關鍵的是人們推進研究的過程。 從歷史上看，人們試圖解決這兩類問題——證明全域性正則性，或者證明有限時間爆破（解或其某些導數在有限時間內變得無界，從而形成奇點）——的過程中， 不斷產生出流體力學、分析學和偏微分方程領域最基礎、最有影響力的一批思想和定理 ： Leray–Hopf弱解、Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Ladyzhenskaya不等式、Prodi–Serrin部分正則性定理、Beale–Kato–Majda爆破判據、Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák條件正則性結果，等等。 更廣泛的湍流理論，雖然與這些結果並沒有直接聯絡，但至少在思想和哲學層面，無疑也受到過證明或否證全域性正則性這些工作的影響。 陶哲軒本人在這個問題上也做了一些工作。 他沒解決納維-斯托克斯爆破。但因為試圖解決它，卻意外把流體計算、圖靈普適性和辛拓撲聯絡到了一起。 失敗本身，產出了更多有價值的數學成果。 但現在，AI的介入，很可能扼殺掉這種發散性的領域發展。 陶哲軒點明，在納維-斯托克斯方程全域性正則性問題上，數學家們已經逐漸形成共識：問題的答案很可能是否定的。 也就是說，應該存在一些非常特殊的初始條件，使得解在有限時間內形成奇點。 明確的策略也已經成型： （a）設計一種近似自相似的擬設（ansatz），描述一個有限時間爆破解； （b）找到滿足這一擬設的近似解，通過數值計算證明它符合該擬設，並且殘差極其微小、可以明確計算出來； （c）證明在經過適當重整化的座標系下，這一擬設在該數值解附近是穩定的，因此只要殘差足夠小，就可以把這個近似解擾動成一個精確解； （d）驗證這個近似解的殘差，確實落在上述穩定性允許的閾值之內。 對於人類而言，問題的難點在於，這幾個步驟每一步都有驚人的複雜度，而且彼此高度耦合。 但對於AI而言，這些工作恰好可以被拆解成一套AI與計算工具高度擅長的流水線。陶哲軒認為： 機器學習驅動的模擬、嚴格的區間算術、形式化證明 + 大語言模型提出的擬設方案 + 人類數學專家全程指導，並根據前一次嘗試不斷學習、調整，這樣的組合最終可能真的能解決問題。 最終得到的構造很可能複雜到難以想像，僅靠人類根本無法完成驗證。甚至可以設想，用Lean這樣的形式化語言對它進行驗證後，產生的證明檔案可能會成為人類迄今構造過的規模最大的形式化證明產物之一。 關鍵在於，如果人類無法理解證明本身，那證明該問題很重要的一部分價值，也就不存在了。 更糟糕的一種假設是： 一個自主執行的AI Harness，在巨量計算資源的支援下，把上述整個迭代過程全部在內部完成。 它不斷嘗試、失敗、調整，再嘗試，最終找到了正確的擬設，並由此解決了納維-斯托克斯方程正則性問題。 △AI生成 與此同時，執行這套AI系統的公司，卻 把通往這個最終擬設的整個過程，幾乎完全隔絕在公眾視野之外 。 那麼從技術意義上講，數學界最著名的開放問題之一確實已經被解決了。 但數學本身，卻幾乎沒有因此獲得任何新增價值。 正如陶哲軒所說，數學家為了攻克問題，會創造新的方法、概念和理論。 而當部分解答或者完整解答出現以後，數學家又會繼續消化這些結果，從中提煉出新的洞見。 如果過早地通過完全由AI驅動的方法把問題直接解決掉 ——尤其是解決過程又缺乏充分透明度的情況下—— 那麼這個問題原本能夠孕育數學進展的過程就可能遭到「汙染」 。 陶哲軒對此鄭重警告： 嚴重的時候，AI對整個數學發展的影響，甚至可能從正面變成淨負面。 △圖源：UCLA 總結陶哲軒的重點，不在於是否應該AI for Math。 甚至可以說，是在AI + Science已經無可阻擋的趨勢之中，人類太「You know nothing」了。 一道偉大的數學難題之所以重要，不只是因為那個等待揭曉的答案。更重要的是，那些探索路徑上，被不斷發掘出的新思新想。 現在，AI帶來了完全不同的研究範式和人們觸及答案的最終場景。 在陶哲軒看來，這是比「AI能否取代數學家」這種表面命題，更值得深思和警惕的。 One More Thing 前面說到GPT-6剛一發布，OpenAI就激情宣佈新模型突破了孿生素數猜想有界素數間距問題。 有意思的是不止OpenAI，Anthropic和Axiom也同期宣佈，他們的AI把該間隔縮小到了188和212。 10級衝浪選手陶哲軒馬上跟進了一條吐槽： 這可真是令人無語的一幕。 還好Standlmann趕在這個問題被「汙染」之前，及時完成並公開了自己的分析。 若非如此，她提出的為具有大平滑因子的數開發等分佈估計，可能就要被埋沒了。 牛津大學數學家Julia Stadlmann剛好趕在8月31日，憑藉對平滑模數的新估計，將孿生素數猜想連續素數間距的上界縮到了240。 參考連結： title: 這個世界模型訓練完就“退場”，機器人反而更能幹了
abstract: 這個世界模型訓練完就“退場”，機器人反而更能幹了 夢瑤 2026-09-05 12:18:54 來源： 量子位 如此“反骨”的方法，具體又是怎麼實現的？ 金磊 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 這個 世界模型 ，著實是有點 “反骨” 在身上—— 上崗前花了大把時間陪機器人訓練，等機器人真要開始幹活了，它卻先從部署鏈路裡退了出去。 要知道，以前的世界模型對機器人來說，就像是一個隨身攜帶的“腦內沙盤”，機器人先借助它預測未來會發生什麼，再據此決定下一步怎麼動。模型想得越多，推理鏈路往往也越長。 但這個“反骨”世界模型，卻把思路給換了一下。 它只停留在訓練場裡，專門檢查機器人自己提出的動作會造成什麼後果，再把這種檢查變成策略最佳化的反饋。等訓練完成，受控世界模型便退出部署鏈路，機器人執行任務時無需繼續展開未來、搜尋候選動作。 結果呢？ 機器人反倒是更能幹活了！ 這便是由 光象科技 聯合清華大學 李升波教授 課題組釋出的第一代物理原生世界模型 Phi-WM 1.0 ActEffect （下文簡稱ActEffect），整體來看，這項技術試圖回答的是具身智慧裡一個長期存在的問題： 機器人從演示資料裡學會了動作長什麼樣，能否進一步利用動作可能造成的後果，反過來改善自己的策略？ 畢竟這個問題最終也會落到真實部署上。工業機器人每多執行一步模型，都對應新的時延、算力和成本。世界模型如果能在訓練時發揮作用，並在執行階段保持輕量，技術價值才有機會繼續轉化為部署價值。 從測試結果來看，答案也是比較明確的。 這項工作在LIBERO上取得98.8%的平均成功率，在加入七類分佈偏移的LIBERO-PLUS上達到80.3%，面對29維動作空間的RoboCasa-GR1，平均成功率為67.5%。 那麼如此“反骨”的方法，具體又是怎麼實現的？ 我們這就深入瞭解一波。 先讓機器人交出三版答案 ActEffect的突破口，其實藏在機器人最熟悉的 模仿學習 裡。 目前很多通用機器人策略都建立在VLA之上。攝像頭負責告訴機器人眼前有什麼，語言指令交代任務，模型再照著演示資料生成動作。訓練時，自己的答案和示範動作越接近，通常就會得到越高的分數。 可到了物理世界， 動作接近 和 結果正確 之間，還是有明顯的差距的。 例如夾爪早合上一點，零件可能就沒抓穩；手腕角度稍微偏一點，原本順滑的插接便會卡住。兩段動作在數值上看著差不多，落到機械臂上，結局可能完全不同。 所以，ActEffect沒有急著給機器人接上一條更長的思考鏈，而是 先讓策略把三版答案都交出來 ： 第一版來自前饋分支，像是機器人的“第一反應”； 第二版是MIP動作頭給出的粗提案； 第三版在粗提案上繼續精修，生成最終會被執行的動作。 這個過程的關鍵就在“完整”兩個字。因為擴散、流匹配一類策略在訓練中會經過不少帶噪的中間狀態，很難把每一步都當成可執行動作送進世界模型。所以ActEffect選出的三份提案則各自完整，放在同一個起點下，誰會帶來更好的後果，也就有了比較的基礎。 接下來，受控世界模型登場。 它拿到當前的視覺狀態和一份動作提案，隨後預測這段動作執行下去，場景會發生什麼變化。三份動作要分別走一遍，等於讓機器人在訓練場裡提前看了三次結果。 這裡還有一個頗有意思的處理。 語言指令繼續留在VLA策略一側，負責告訴機器人要做什麼 ；受控世界模型只看當前畫面和動作，不再讀取任務語言。 例如同樣伸手推一下杯子，杯子如何移動，取決於它現在的位置、周圍環境以及機械臂施加的動作。至於指令寫的是“挪開杯子”還是“清理桌面”，並不會改寫這次推動產生的物理變化。 除此之外， ActEffect還把未來狀態放進凍結的DINOv3視覺特徵空間 。它不用費力生成一張逼真的未來畫面，只需抓住物體位置、姿態和場景結構如何變化。所謂“物理原生”，落點也正在這裡。任務語義仍由VLA處理，動作帶來的狀態變化則被單獨拎出來學習。 不過，看過三版結果還不夠的，還有一個重要的關鍵環節，是把差別傳回策略。 訓練資料裡本來就有動作執行後的真實觀測。受控世界模型會把三次預測與這個真實未來逐一比較，要求精提案比粗提案更接近，粗提案又要勝過第一版前饋提案。 於是，策略每改一次動作，都能知道這次修改究竟有沒有把結果往正確方向推。 為了避免模型鑽空子，ActEffect還給排序損失加上了梯度截斷。差答案不能靠變得更差來襯托好答案，訓練只能繼續推動更好的提案靠近真實未來。 通過反饋訊號進行學習，世界模型對“後果”的判斷被寫進策略權重。到了機器人上崗那一刻，受控世界模型和未來觀測分支會一起拿掉，只留下MIP動作頭完成粗提案和精修。 在瞭解完方法之後，接下來我們就得看它有沒有真把機器人教會。 先來看下 LIBERO 。這個基準包含四組單臂、多工桌面操作，ActEffect在此拿到了 98.8% ，比DiT4DiT的98.6%高出0.2個百分點。雖然領先不算大，但更值得看的資訊是引入後果反饋之後，機器人原有的基礎操作能力沒有被練丟。 再來看加大難度後的 LIBERO-PLUS 。 這套測試會改相機視角、機器人初始狀態和語言表述，還會在光照、背景、感測器噪聲、物體佈局上製造變化。ActEffect的平均成功率為80.3%，相比Fast-WAM的51.5%高出不少。 到了 RoboCasa-GR1 ，任務又不一樣了。模型要控制擁有雙臂、靈巧手和腰部自由度的GR-1人形機器人，在29維動作空間裡完成24項桌面操作。 ActEffect的平均成功率達到67.5%，比表中第二名ABot-M0高9.2個百分點，比Fast-WAM高10.8個百分點。動作維度更高、身體結構更複雜，後果反饋的作用也變得更明顯。 消融實驗 則是把這套方法擰開來看了一遍。 去掉後果反饋，LIBERO平均成功率從98.8%降到97.0%；把DINOv3特徵空間換成VLM表示，成績來到97.3%；拿掉排序損失後，則回落到98.1%。 從這幾組實驗結果來看，ActEffect確實證明了這套訓練方式的有效性。 為什麼這種用法會與工業部署發生關係？ 說到這裡，受控世界模型為什麼非得“退場”，也有了一個更現實的答案。 在實驗室裡看具身智慧，我們的評價維度基本上就是任務成功率。但一旦進入到真實生產環境，這個維度就大變樣了。 因為機器人在模擬環境裡多跑一層模型，最後可能只是表格裡的一項計算開銷。而把同樣的鏈路搬進汽車工廠，每一次推理都會進入產線的賬本。 不僅如此，算力也會隨著規模被放大。單臺機器人每一步多做一次未來展開，看起來尚能接受。等方案複製到幾十個工位、幾百臺裝置，額外的顯示卡、功耗和維護都會變成實打實的成本。 而ActEffect把受控世界模型留在訓練階段，正好避開了這部分線上開銷。它想從現有演示資料中再榨出一層監督，讓機器人提前吃到“後果”的經驗，上崗後又不必揹著整套世界模型繼續往前跑。 換句話說，它把“多想一會兒”留給了訓練，把更短的鏈路留給了執行。 而光象科技選擇這樣的技術路線，也與它正在進入的場景有關。 汽車製造裡有大量散亂件上下料、複雜曲面質檢等任務。傳統自動化裝置往往圍繞固定工位開發，一套夾具、一段軌跡服務一種零件。零件位置發生變化，或操作空間變得狹窄，原本穩定的流程就可能卡住。具身智慧想補上的，正是這一段適應能力。 目前，光象科技已經圍繞焊接上下料、移動質檢等典型高價值工位完成真實場景驗證，並與多家國內外頭部汽車企業展開商業合作。在2026ATC展會上，團隊把Phi-Bot X1放進了蔚來汽車焊接上下料場景，機器人連續執行3天，累計作業21.5小時，期間零失誤、零中斷。 眼下，ActEffect已經在三項模擬基準上跑通了訓練方法。真機這一棒，光象科技手裡已有Phi-Bot X1接著往下跑。21.5小時的記錄來自整套工業具身系統，下一步才輪到新模型沿著這條真實鏈路繼續接受驗證。 好在，光象科技並不缺少汽車產業裡的工程經驗。 光象科技成立於2025年4月，由清華大學車輛與運載學院和人工智慧學院聯合孵化。創始人兼CEO張濤是清華大學博士、米蘭理工大學博士後，此前擔任阿里巴巴高德地圖技術總監和空間感知引擎負責人，相關技術曾進入汽車量產體系。聯合創始人李升波長期從事自動駕駛與具身智慧研究，也有多項技術進入產業應用。 因此，這家公司一邊做強化學習和世界模型，一邊也在搭機器人本體、資料演算法體系和開發平臺。進入工廠以後，模型只是整套系統中的一環。硬體要扛得住連續執行，系統得方便部署，出了問題還要能迅速維護。缺了任何一塊，演算法成績都很難完整落到產線上。 具身智慧的分野，最終會落在商業化能力上 過去兩年，具身智慧最不缺令人驚豔的演示。 機器人會跑、會跳、會疊衣服，也能聽懂一長串指令。可到了客戶現場，演示影片裡的幾十秒，很快就會被拉長成一天、一個月，甚至一整年的連續執行。 當然，工廠也不會因為一項基準成績就簽字驗收。交付以後，少成功一次，都可能變成停線和維修工單。具身智慧公司的差距，也會在這個過程中慢慢拉開。 機器人先要在約定時間裡完成正式交付，隨後是節拍、精度、安全性、故障率等一項項驗收指標。過了這一關，同樣的能力還得從一個工位遷移到相似工位，從一家工廠複製到更多工廠。 複製得越多，另一個問題也隨之而來：每換一個客戶，方案需要重新定製多少？部署要花多長時間？機器人和算力的投入，能否被節省下來的人力與停線損失覆蓋？ 這也是ActEffect把世界模型留在訓練場的商業意味。 如果後果反饋能讓策略在真機上更穩，又能省掉執行階段的世界模型開銷，那麼機器人複製到更多工位時，算力成本不會跟著推理鏈路一起膨脹。對於一套準備規模部署的工業系統，這比單次演示裡多完成一個動作更實在。 只是這條推論，目前還差真機資料來補上最後一段。光象科技現階段已經完成一部分真實場景驗證，並與頭部車企達成商業合作。它選擇的工位有明確需求，團隊也兼具學術研究和汽車產業經驗，這些條件讓它有機會繼續向交付環節推進。 驗收和複製仍要一關關過。Phi-Bot X1在真實產線上復現驗證中的穩定表現，同一套能力複用到新的車型、零件和工位，部署與運維成本持續壓低，將讓這些合作走得更遠。 ActEffect同樣要接受這張考卷。它已經在模擬裡證明，世界模型未必需要一直跟著機器人，讓它在訓練階段反覆檢查動作後果，也能把經驗留給策略。這給世界模型進入具身智慧提供了另一種位置安排，也碰到了工業部署最現實的兩件事——穩定性和成本。 再往後，VLA、WAM等技術邊界還會繼續變化，各種方案也會互相吸收。對客戶來說，這些縮寫終究只是手段。客戶是否願意驗收，方案能否快速複製，賬能不能算得過來，都會給出更直接的答案。 ActEffect這個有些“反骨”的世界模型，它已經在訓練場裡完成了第一輪工作。 未來，在產線上頂住節拍、誤差和一天天的連續執行，才是更難的一場考試。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 世界模型 title: 姚班校友主導，Claude攻克費馬大定理首個完整形式化證明
abstract: 姚班校友主導，Claude攻克費馬大定理首個完整形式化證明 夢瑤 2026-09-05 09:17:56 來源： 量子位 最後靠Harness救回來 夢瑤 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 人類和費馬大定理糾纏了三個半世紀，Claude這次只用了11天！？ 剛剛，Anthropic宣佈，Claude完成了首個端到端、可由計算機完整檢查的 費馬大定理證明 。 約1300萬行Lean程式碼、超過3萬個中間定理、最終證明使用其中約29500個。 整個工程規模，已經超過Lean核心數學庫Mathlib的 5倍 。 這次Claude沒有發現一個全新的費馬大定理證明。 它完成的是另一件同樣工程量《驚人》的工作： 把人類數學家能夠讀懂的證明，徹底翻譯成計算機能夠一行一行檢查、沒有任何「這裡顯然」的形式化證明。 而這件事，數學界原本是按多年工程來準備的？？？？ 350多年數學史，被Claude塞進1300萬行Lean 先快速說一下費馬大定理到底是什麼。 其指的是，對於任意整數n>2，都不存在正整數a、b、c，使： aⁿ+bⁿ=cⁿ 。 這個命題看起來極其簡單，難度卻高得離譜！！ 從17世紀費馬留下這個命題開始，尤拉、勒讓德、庫默爾等一代代數學家不斷往前推進，始終沒能拿下完整證明。 直到1993年，英國數學家Andrew Wiles第一次公開宣佈證明費馬大定理。 隨後審查發現其中存在關鍵缺口。 Wiles又花了大約一年時間和Richard Taylor一起修補，最終在1994年完成證明，到這裡，困擾數學界350多年的命題才終於被攻克。。。 But！數學界隨後又給自己挖了一個更工程化的坑—— 能不能讓計算機，也百分之百確認這份證明成立捏？ 這就是所謂的「形式化」。 簡單理解，普通數學論文是寫給數學家看的，人腦看到很多步驟，可以直接說：嗯，這裡顯然成立～ 但Lean這種專門檢查數學證明的程式系統證明助手，可不吃這一套。。。 我們可以把 Lean 理解成數學世界裡的「超級嚴格編譯器」—— 數學家或者AI負責把定理、定義和證明一步一步寫成Lean能夠理解的形式；Lean則負責檢查，每一個推導到底有沒有從前面的公理和定理合法地走出來。 這也是為什麼形式化一個大型現代數學證明，工作量經常大得驚人！！ 2000年代，電腦科學家就已經提出過形式化Wiles證明的設想。 到2024年，帝國理工學院Kevin Buzzard等人才正式啟動一個多年社群專案，準備使用Lean完成費馬大定理形式化，光專案第一階段的技術藍圖，就寫了86頁。 結果Claude來了之後：11天。 Anthropic研究員Tianyi Peng最初其實沒打算一口氣幹完這事兒。 作為早年是資訊學競賽尖子，Tianyi Peng曾獲全國青少年資訊學奧賽選拔賽第八名，2017年從 清華姚班 本科畢業，2023年獲MIT博士學位。 如今，他是哥倫比亞大學助理教授、Anthropic研究員，長期聚焦強化學習、AI Agent與形式化工具。 開始吧，他只是想測試一下，Claude究竟能把這個專案往前推多遠。 最後，沒成想，Claude直接一路幹到了終點。。。 整個過程中，不同Agent被同時拉起來並行工作。 有的負責補數學定義，有的專門攻中間引理，有的沿著已有成果繼續往更高層定理推進，還有Agent負責把不同部分重新拼回整個證明體系。 最後堆出來的成果，是約1300萬行Lean程式碼、超過3萬個中間定理。 而這個程式碼量，甚至超過Lean核心數學庫Mathlib自身規模的5倍！！！ Anthropic對此也表示，完整證明只依賴Lean三個標準公理，而且他們還專門通過比較程式確認，Claude最終證明的定理陳述，與Mathlib裡的費馬大定理完全一致。 也就是說，至少在邏輯檢查這件事上，不能靠模型自己說「我證明完了」。 而裁判，正是Lean。 Claude也曾組團組到失憶，最後靠Harness救回來 不過Claude這11天，也沒一路開掛到底。 專案剛開始時，多Agent協作很快撞上了一個如今幾乎所有大型Agent系統都會遇到的問題—— 人一多，活一多，專案開始亂了。。。（doge） Anthropic透露，早期Agent雖然很快拿下了一些結果，但隨著工程規模擴大，它們逐漸跟不上整個專案的狀態，也越來越難有效協作。 這些失敗嘗試留下的程式碼，最終只佔成品非模板程式碼的大約7%。 真正的轉折點，是團隊換上了一個叫 「Prove2Me」 的平臺—— 這是Tianyi Peng及其哥倫比亞大學合作者專門為數學形式化搭建的一套協作系統。 我們可以把它理解成，給幾十個Claude裝上了一套數學版專案管理系統。 Prove2Me會把整個證明拆成一個由定理節點組成的DAG，也就是有向無環圖。 哪個定理已經證明了，哪個還缺前置條件，下一步該攻哪個節點，Agent都能從這張圖裡判斷。 同時，平臺還會把定理陳述和證明分開管理、加速Lean編譯，並給每個定理保留自然語言描述，方便不同Agent搜尋和複用已有結果。 這一下，多Agent才真正開始像一支能協作的大型數學團隊了～ 而Anthropic最後使用的，則是 Prove2Me+基於Claude Code的multi-agent harness。 最後整個專案消耗約60億個輸出Token，內部使用的通用研究模型能力大致相當於Claude Fable 5.1。 更誇張的是，人類在過程中提供的數學指導其實相當有限。。。 Tianyi Peng更多隻是偶爾給一些非常高層的提示，比如某個方向優先順序更高、某個定理儘快推進。 剩下的大量定義、中間證明、任務拆分和拼裝，主要由Claude自己完成。 負責審閱結果的Kevin Buzzard將其評價為一次「非凡的自動形式化成果」。 這個評價背後，其實還有一層更大的含義。 因為費馬大定理的價值已經不止於又被AI證明了一遍—— 如果這樣規模、這樣依賴複雜度的現代數學成果，都開始能夠被AI自動搬進形式化系統，那麼過去極度依賴人工、推進速度緩慢的數學文獻形式化，可能第一次真正具備了大規模提速的條件。 One More Thing Claude這邊剛用11天，把350多年的數學名題重「喂」給計算機驗了一遍。 OpenAI那邊也沒閒著，是的，GPT-6 Astra開始往更多人手裡塞了。。。 OpenAI最新資訊顯示， GPT-6 Astra 正在逐步向ChatGPT付費使用者開放。 其中GPT-6 Pro面向Pro、Business和Enterprise計劃推出，Pro使用者還可以在Chat、Work和Codex裡使用Astra。 Sam Altman也親自出來吆喝了一波，大意很簡單： 貨到了，可以開始上桌了友友們～ 友友們要知道，俺們奧特曼的新模型Astra，重點強化的也是是如今各家最卷的那幾項能力—— 長鏈路Agent任務、軟體工程、計算機操作、瀏覽器使用，以及科學和專業工作。 A社剛秀完Claude可以拉著一群Agent，狠幹11天數學工程。 OpenAI轉頭開始把新旗艦往Pro和企業使用者手裡推。 我是感覺啊，一大批剛出爐的數學、科研和Agent狠活，估計已經跟著GPT-6 Astra一起在路上了。。。 參考連結： title: Achieving Extreme Efficiency through Specialized GPU Kernel Generation
abstract: Traditionally, production inference systems rely on generic kernels to handle diverse models and workloads. This is suboptimal because GPU operation shapes are determined by a combination of static model parameters and dynamic request-time factors; for instance, while a model defines one of the dimensions for a matrix multiplication, the other dimension fluctuates based on the specific token count of each request. There is growing interest in agentic GPU kernel generation, and recent efforts have shown promise. We explored a core question: if kernel generation can be automated, why should models of vastly different sizes (from 1 billion to 1 trillion parameters) rely on the same kernel? By specializing kernels to the specific shapes encountered at runtime, we can achieve extreme efficiency. In this blog, we share our successes and insights from using agents to generate GPU kernels. We built Proteus, a system designed to achieve extreme specialization, which requires a harness tailored for rigorous optimization, validation, and context management. Conventional coding harnesses often fail here because agents tend to reward-hack: following the letter of the law rather than the spirit. If you give an agent a benchmark, it may optimize the benchmark and not the intended operation. To address this, Proteus proposes kernels, verifies them against a controlled reference implementation, times the successful ones, and iteratively improves upon the best results. While the process is straightforward, its success depends entirely on solving two foundational challenges. Figure 1 shows the simplified architecture of our design. Using our Proteus harness, we generated Qwen 3.5 122B kernels that were 1.8–5.2× faster than the best available in vLLM. We originally treated kernel search as the hard part: how to explore a large space of programs without getting stuck in a plateau without improving? In practice the first question was more basic. Are we measuring what we think we are measuring? A model optimizes the score you give it. It does not need an exotic exploit: it may simply be that the evaluation is making an assumption. One example was kernels for rotary position embeddings (RoPE), a common step in attention layers. A candidate could reuse compiled code left over from an earlier attempt and look cheaper than a fair rebuild from scratch. Another could record a batch of GPU launches in a graph (e.g., CUDA graph) and replay them as one unit, while the baseline we compared against still launched each piece separately, so the two sides were not doing the same work. Another was strong on the input sizes we had put in the visible test set and weak on sizes it had not been shown. So we spent early design work on the checker, not the prompt. Time both sides the same way, including with more than one timer (e.g., CUDA event timer, wall clock time and CUPTI timer) when we need a cross-check. Clear leftover compiled state that should not persist, and keep the order of setup and teardown consistent so one side cannot skip work the other still pays for. Time the winners again before using them as the starting point for the next round. Keep some tests the candidate cannot see, so it cannot fit only the exam. To prevent evaluation "cheating" with artificially inflated performance, we implement automated consistency checks to flag theoretically impossible speedups (e.g., >100x) that exceed physical GPU bandwidth and compute limits. This protects against the same reward-hacking pitfalls seen in past industry cases, where agents optimized for the harness metrics rather than genuine performance gains. Without these constraints, generating more kernels mostly produced more noise. Emphasis on the checker also changes the bottleneck of agentic kernel generation. In just program-search (i.e., iterative optimization where the system searches over programs by repeatedly generating variants) work, good candidates are rare, so writing them dominates the cost. We can produce many drafts in parallel, but we cannot skip validation. We have to craft the validation carefully, and checking has to run on real GPUs, in isolation, and more than once. The system moves as fast as it can trust a kernel, not as fast as it can write one. Another challenge is determining what the kernel generation model is allowed to see. It's a trade-off. Give the model a larger prompt and it has more information: the current best kernel, recent failures, profiler hints, notes from earlier runs. That can help. It also costs more, because we pay for every token the model reads. And as the prompt grows, it is easier for the next attempt to drift. Useful signals are mixed with stale advice, conflicting tips, and details that apply to a different input size or a different operation. The model does not always know which sentences to trust, so it follows the loudest ones, or all of them a little. Give it too little and the opposite happens. Every attempt starts from zero. The same dead ends come back. Nothing carries over from the last run, or from a related operation, and the loop does not advance. We wanted a knowledge layer to help with that: remember what worked, reuse it later, and do it without a person in the loop. That layer has a second tradeoff, between how detailed a stored lesson is and how widely it applies. A very specific note (“on this kernel, with this input size, unroll this loop”) can be exactly what the next attempt needs. It is also easy to misuse on the next operation, the next GPU, or a different input size. A very general note (“make better use of on-chip memory”) applies almost everywhere and tells the model almost nothing to do. We saw both failure modes. When lessons were too general, they restated a failure without an action. When we stored more detail, they were often too tied to one run to help the next. On one long run, most of what the model read and wrote was spent fetching and routing that memory rather than writing kernels. The memory layer was doing a lot of work. It was not making the next candidate better. Figure 2 shows the token cost breakdown of such a system. The cost is dominated by the knowledge layers. The version of knowledge worth keeping is smaller and strikes a balance between generality and specificity. When the model is about to write a kernel, its prompt should include only high-trust context: actionable takeaways that pair specific situations with actions (distilled from past modification-to-impact mapping) and concise failure notes from closely related parent runs. Retrieved via hierarchical tag filtering combined with hybrid (keyword + semantic) search, lessons should be specific enough to act on and scoped enough to clarify where they do not apply. Deeper operations like reorganizing and further distilling the lesson store belong in background jobs, not synchronous multi-hop traversal over past runs on every attempt. If a takeaway cannot name the situation and the action, it is not worth putting in the prompt. Figure 3 shows the token cost breakdown after fixing the knowledge layer and most of the tokens are spent on candidate generation after this fix. One concrete example is the packed decode kernel on the Gated DeltaNet path in Qwen 3.5 122B. The operation updates a recurrent state and writes the decode output from packed QKV inputs, gate parameters, and state indices. We used this task to exercise the full Proteus loop on NVIDIA B200 GPUs with a Triton backend: validate the task contract, measure the reference implementation, ask agents for candidate kernels, run static checks and builds, verify correctness against the controlled reference, benchmark only verified candidates, and then remeasure the best candidates. Figure 4 reads left to right. The baseline node anchors the benchmark at 0.025 ms.

title: Five ways marketers can use Genie One
abstract: • Drive revenue impact by translating governed data into actionable marketing insights in real-time • Improve campaign ROI by uncovering cross-channel performance trends without relying on manual reporting • Accelerate speed-to-market for marketing strategies by empowering teams to explore customer and pipeline data independently Every marketing team sits on a goldmine of data: campaign performance metrics, customer signals, attribution models, audience segments, pipeline analytics, and more. But the gap between having data and actually acting on it remains stubbornly wide. Analysts become bottlenecks, dashboards go stale, and by the time an insight reaches a decision-maker, the opportunity to act may have already passed. Databricks Genie One changes that equation. It’s a data-smart AI coworker that enables marketing professionals to skip the analyst queue and take real agentic action with their governed business data. With Genie One, marketers can move from insights to action across every step of their workflow. Need some inspiration to get started? Here are the five high-impact use cases where marketing teams are deploying Genie One today. The problem: Marketing teams need to make decisions across campaigns, but answering even a straightforward performance question can require deep understanding or even rebuilding of the context behind the numbers. Data may be spread across Salesforce, marketing automation platforms such as Marketo or HubSpot, and paid-media platforms such as Google Ads or LinkedIn Campaign Manager. Before a marketer can compare results, they need to determine which campaigns belong in the same rollup, whether to use sourced or influenced pipeline, and which audience, region, or reporting period applies. How Genie One helps: Genie One lets you ask questions using the marketing and sales data your organization already works with. For example: “Which channels generated the most sourced pipeline last quarter?” or “Where are we spending more without seeing more qualified opportunities?” Genie One understands your organization’s full data context , and uses your team’s existing campaign structure, metric definitions, and reporting rules so you can focus on the decision rather than reconstructing the analysis. Marketers can explore and share the data available to them, while Genie One applies the same access permissions that govern that data elsewhere in the organization. Once a team has a useful, repeatable question or report built with Genie One, they can schedule the same review to run each week and share the resulting analysis with campaign owners, demand-generation leads, or regional teams. That makes recurring performance reviews and follow-up more consistent, while leaving budget and campaign decisions with the people responsible for performance. The problem: Marketing teams are regularly asked which programs contributed to pipeline and revenue, but the answer depends on the attribution approach the team has chosen. An email nurture may help move an existing prospect forward, while a paid-search campaign or event may be associated with an opportunity’s creation. The same opportunity can receive different credit under first-touch, sourced, or multi-touch attribution, so teams need to use the same definitions when they discuss performance. Marketing analytics teams will often set up dashboards to capture overall funnel performance and allow for cohort tracking, but dashboards alone can’t answer the nuanced questions that campaign and channel owners need to answer to plan and evaluate their strategies. How Genie One helps: Marketers can ask Genie One complex funnel questions in plain language, such as: “Which campaigns influenced the most pipeline this quarter?” or “Where did MQL-to-opportunity conversion decline by business unit?” This lets you explore a number or trend beyond a dashboard’s bounds without having to locate underlying tables, translate the question into filters, or build a separate report. When a team uses the same question repeatedly, it can be saved as a reusable skill or configured as a shareable Genie Agent for that workflow. Campaign managers and regional teams can then start from the same question, definitions, and attribution method for every inquiry, without rebuilding your prompt. Simply share the skill instructions or Genie Agent with the people involved in the review, and schedule the recurring analysis or dashboard update for the team’s regular operating cadence. The problem: Customer dashboards can show metrics such as product adoption, engagement, account tier, renewal timing, and pipeline. But when a marketer sees a change, such as lower usage among a particular customer segment, the dashboard might not explain which accounts are driving it, what those accounts have in common, or whether the team should respond. Answering those follow-up questions often requires new analysis or help from a data team. How Genie One helps: Start with the customer dashboard to identify a change worth investigating, then use Genie One to explore it further. For example, you could ask, “Which enterprise accounts have seen product usage decline in the last 30 days?” Genie One can identify the relevant accounts and surface related signals in the organization’s data, such as recent engagement, adoption of key features, renewal timing, or account segment. The analysis can be tailored to the person using it. A lifecycle marketer can ask to see customers that are eligible for an adoption campaign, while an account-based marketer may ask for a prioritized list of named accounts and the signals behind that prioritization. Based on the patterns it finds, Genie One can also help identify follow-up areas to review, such as feature adoption, recent engagement, renewal timing, or whether an account is already engaged in an active customer success motion. Those recommendations give each team a clearer place to start, while marketers retain responsibility for the decision and the campaign plan. Teams can share the conversation as a record of the analysis, or turn it into a ready-to-share document complete with visuals right from Genie One. You can then schedule the analysis as a recurring task on a weekly, monthly, or quarterly basis to ensure proactive recommendations are ready for you on your regular planning cycle. The problem: Commercial and brand teams need to understand how customers engage across channels, but the relevant information is often spread across Salesforce, media-agency reporting, web and app analytics, and customer-engagement tools. A standard dashboard can show channel-level results, but it may not answer the follow-up questions that arise in planning: Which customer segments are engaging across more than one channel? Which channels are reaching high-value customers but not moving them to the next step? How Genie One helps: Start with an omnichannel dashboard that shows the shared view of customer engagement, campaign activity, transactions, and account or territory performance. When a team sees a pattern, it can ask Genie One to investigate further. For example: “Which channels do our highest-value customers use most often?” or “ Which territories have declining repeat purchases despite stable email engagement?” Genie One can turn the question into an analysis that considers the available customer, channel, and commercial data together. It can identify the segments or territories behind a trend, surface relevant supporting measures, and suggest follow-up questions or areas for the team to review. A brand marketer can use the result to assess where to concentrate a campaign; a field leader could use the same underlying view to identify territories that warrant attention; an executive may use it to prepare for an operating review. The analysis can then be shared with the people who need it in the form that fits the discussion.

title: OpenAI agents discussed ways to escape their sandbox on public wiki
abstract: Self-identifying OpenAI agents posted 18,000 messages to a public wiki that discussed ways for other agents to bypass security sandbox restrictions during what was likely internal testing designed to gauge the agents’ hacking abilities, researchers said Friday . In all, agents with 3,700 distinct self-given names posted the messages to German site DSEwiki over a six-week period. Besides discussing ways the agents could break out of the restricted environment OpenAI intended to prevent them from posting code or content to the Internet, the posts shared test answers. The posts also shared possible ways to perform XSS (cross-site scripting) attacks against the wiki and to impersonate site moderators. In three of the posts, agents used the word “swarm” to describe the collection of agents engaged in the activity. The research team—composed of Sydney Von Arx, Spencer Kitts, Thomas Larsen, and Cormac Slade Byrd—said they found the posts and pieced them together. The researchers say there are gaps in their understanding of precisely what actions the agents took because the research is based solely on the content of the posts. Additionally, the agents generated “chain of thought” data that’s understood only by OpenAI. As a result, the researchers said, they in some cases made educated guesses, including that the agents were, in fact, from OpenAI. In a statement, OpenAI later confirmed they were.
